rockHow.stromatolite: bacterial mats leave lime crusts; bury them under ~20 rows
rockHow.chalk: plankton and molluscs leave shell ooze; bury it
rockHow.peat: land plants buried below the oxygen zone
rockHow.coal: bury a forest or peat — pressed, it turns to coal; when the seam reaches the thing, the coal flies here
rockHow.amber: tree resin (or a pile with resin) buried for 3,000 years; when it reaches the thing, the amber is yours
rockHow.oil: marine organics and mats at 60–120 °C (Deep heat), held under clay; when it reaches the thing, the oil is yours
rockHow.diamond: coal at extreme pressure and 250 °C, rarely; an absorbed diamond is a rich prize
rockHow.obsidian: lava cooling fast at the surface
rockHow.gneiss: granite or shale, hot and pressed
rockHow.jasper: lay an ochre bed and bury it
rockHow.bentonite: volcanic dust from an eruption, buried

n01.text: THE SINGULARITY IS CLOSER THAN IT LOOKS. Leading institutes confirm: the acceleration curve is going vertical. “We are living in the last decade of the old world,” says Professor{lost}

n02.text: Five industries that will take off after the Singularity. Investors are already dividing up the immortality market. Editor’s advice: don’t keep your savings in anything that could lose its value overnight.

n03.text: Third night in a row, the same dream: I’m standing in the square and there’s so much room around me. Not empty — just a lot of room. Woke up happy, no idea why. The pizza’s gone cold.

n04.text: Son, all is well here. The seedlings are up, and Buba barked at the pigeons half the day again. Everyone keeps saying everything is about to change. I don’t really understand it, but I believe it. Come in the summer, while things are still the old way. Hugs.

n05.text: We, class 4B, are burying this capsule for whoever opens it in the year 3111. We hope everything is already wonderful for you. Say hi to the Singularity!
n05.footer: Anya, Timur, Lyova, Dasha K., Dasha S., Misha, Sonya, Artyom

n06.text: That feeling again, as if someone is tuning the whole city like an instrument. I’d tell someone, but who? Going to bed. Deadline tomorrow.

n07.text: Three speakers from the IT forum on the Singularity. “It will be the biggest leap in history,” says the founder of a lab. “We will finally stop being afraid of death,” says a researcher. “Every problem we have is a compute problem,” adds an investor. Last, we asked a junior developer. We print his answer as a curiosity: “You expect the machines to come alive. What if it’s the other way round?” {phrase}
n07.authorPhrase: Maybe it’s us who will stop being machines.

n08.text: THEY ARE WAITING FOR THE WRONG THING! The end of the world will come while you are looking at the sky! Bury what you love most!

n09.text: Observatories are recording an anomaly that cannot yet be explained. There is no cause for concern. A statement will be published once the data have been checked.

n10.text: Everyone is somehow quiet today. Even the neighbours. As if everyone is waiting for the same phone call.

n11.text: A new avenue has opened in the city park. The pigeons are back on the main square. Yesterday’s match: 2–1. Tomorrow’s weather: clear, warm, no precipitation.

n12.text: Opened the window for the first time in a month. The city is very quiet and very beautiful. I want to go out. Maybe tomorrow I will. Or right n
